facts.raw_span: A 44-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance
he had a history of hypertension
he had a history of cervical disc herniation
he underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale
his father had progressive cognitive decline and imbalance since the age of 50 years
his father died of cerebral hemorrhage at the age of 65 years
Neurological examination revealed brisk bilateral tendon reflexes
bilateral Babinski sign
T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery showing lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities (WMH)
a lobe-dominant distribution of multiple cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) and relatively fewer CMBs in deep regions, mainly involving bilateral parieto-occipital lobes
a heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene
2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance

concepts.why: The patient's cerebral microbleeds, lacunar infarctions, and periventricular white matter hyperintensities, along with the HTRA1 gene mutation, suggest Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy.
The patient's history of hypertension, along with the presence of lacunar infarctions and cerebral microbleeds, suggests Hypertensive Angiopathy.

aliases: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy
concepts.why: The patient's family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance, along with the HTRA1 gene mutation, suggests CADASIL Syndrome.
The patient's lacunar infarctions, periventricular white matter hyperintensities, and cerebral microbleeds suggest Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
The patient's family history of cerebral hemorrhage, along with the HTRA1 gene mutation and cerebral microbleeds, suggests Hereditary Cerebral Hemorrhage with Amyloidosis.
The patient's history of cognitive decline, along with the presence of lacunar infarctions and cerebral microbleeds, suggests Vascular Dementia.

rationales.F01: The patient's symptoms are non-specific and could be related to various conditions.
rationales.F06: The family history of cerebral hemorrhage suggests a possible hereditary component.
rationales.F09: The presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities is consistent with cerebral small vessel disease.
rationales.F10: The lobe-dominant distribution of cerebral microbleeds is suggestive of cerebral amyloid angiopathy.
rationales.F11: The mutation in the HTRA1 gene is not typically associated with CADASIL syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance, along with the presence of a heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene, strongly supports CADASIL Syndrome as the most likely diagnosis.
